qa.answer: Four options. Hold Kansai with a Jurong standby PO and move the turbine oil line to Rheinland (saves USD 1.5K, no slip, recommended), buy the blast media from Jurong now (USD 2.1K, no slip), wait for the Kansai restart (no cost, no slip unless inspections run long), or air expedite from Sakai on restart (USD 2K, no slip, depends on the restart date).

The recommended option is the cheapest: Rheinland turbine oil is USD 26 against Kansai's USD 28, saving USD 1,464 on 732 units. The Jurong standby only costs the USD 7 per unit premium, USD 2.1K in total, if Kansai misses the 13 Oct trigger. Waiting for the restart costs nothing but carries no fallback.

In 2024 a typhoon closed two north Taiwan fastener plants for 8 days (PRE-06), and we pulled forward from US distributor stock at a 35% premium to hold two heavy checks. Here the local Jurong premium on blast media is about 16% and the float is wider, which is why the recommendation parks the local buy as a standby rather than placing it now.

The induction does not move. WO-2613 needs 300 units of blast media on 19 Oct and Kansai's post-inspection ETA is 20 Oct, a 1 day slip against 5 days of float, so Monsoonal Air's 9 Nov redelivery holds. It would only move if inspections ran past roughly 13 Oct without a local fallback in place.
